description: Sotto v2: a voice in the room. Sotto answers out loud via ElevenLabs when addressed (fast acknowledgment, no length cap), can be interrupted by saying 'Sotto', ignores its own voice, greets the room, researches in the background with sourced packets and quiet research-ready cards plus spoken briefings, gates candidates with Muse Glimmer running locally (Spark fallback), adds frequency/boldness controls and an end-of-session digest. Unprompted contributions stay on screen. Full spec: tasks/prd-sotto-v2.md (wins over tasks/prd-sotto-core.md where they disagree).

userStories.title: ElevenLabs speech service
userStories.description: As the system, I need to turn text into streaming speech quickly, stop it instantly, and know exactly what was spoken.
acceptanceCriteria: server/voice/Speaker.ts streams text to ElevenLabs input-streaming WebSocket (/v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}/stream-input), model eleven_flash_v2_5, output pcm_24000, emitting audio chunks as they arrive (check https://elevenlabs.io/docs for the current protocol)
Accepts text incrementally (sentence by sentence) so speech starts before the full text exists
Requests alignment data and tracks which characters have been played, so after a stop the exact spoken-so-far text is known
cancel() stops the stream immediately and discards pending audio
Voice from ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID, else a documented calm default library voice
Unit tests with a mocked ElevenLabs socket: incremental text, cancel mid-stream, spoken-so-far tracking
Integration test (real API): one sentence yields non-empty PCM; time to first audio chunk logged

userStories.title: Self-echo suppression
userStories.description: As a user, I don't want Sotto's own voice in the transcript, on the board, or triggering anything.
acceptanceCriteria: During playback and 1.5 s after, transcribed turns that fuzzy-match (token overlap >= 0.6) text Sotto spoke in that window are marked selfEcho and excluded from transcript, board, observer, wake detection and session files (logged to timing.jsonl only)
Wake detections matching Sotto's own recent speech (e.g. its hello saying 'I'm Sotto') are ignored
Non-matching turns during playback (side talk) stay in the transcript but trigger no wake question, interjection delivery or research (barge-in is V2-007)
Pure, unit-tested matcher: exact echo, partial echo, echo with ASR errors, unrelated side talk, side talk quoting a few of Sotto's words
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Barge-in and follow-ups
userStories.description: As a participant, I want to cut Sotto off by saying its name, and redirect or resume it.
acceptanceCriteria: While speaking, wake detection runs on PARTIAL turns; a valid detection immediately cancels speech (Speaker cancel + browser flush); wake-word-end-to-silence latency is computed from transcription audio positions and logged to timing.jsonl (target < 1.5 s)
Optional ducking: a non-echo human speech partial during playback drops volume to 30% until the turn resolves; restored if not a barge-in

After the turn is final, the command is classified (structured output): stop ('Sotto, stop' / 'thanks Sotto') -> silence; new_question -> answer it; continue ('Sotto, go on') -> resume from spokenSoFar
Interrupted answers are recorded with spokenSoFar, and follow-up context tells the model it was cut off
Unit tests on a simulated clock: barge-in on a partial stops playback; each command type; barge-in during the acknowledgment; stop then new question
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: HUMAN CHECKPOINT: live voice test
userStories.description: As the team, we need to confirm in a real room that echo cancellation and barge-in work before building on them.
acceptanceCriteria: The loop does not start this story until tasks/checkpoint-voice.md exists (ralph.sh enforces this)

userStories.title: Research planner and gate
userStories.description: As the system, I want to decide what's worth researching, from explicit hooks and from the conversation itself, without researching everything.
acceptanceCriteria: Research ideas come from research_hook candidates and from a planner run every 2 minutes (injected Clock) when >= 3 new final turns arrived; the planner asks Muse Spark for <= 2 concrete, checkable items given board + recent turns; prompt server/prompts/research-planner.md with examples across business, scheduling, cooking, technical topics (no per-topic playbooks)

userStories.title: Glimmer as the judgment gate
